findings.reason: a node applies both exemptions, reruns the family, and finds those two ids still red with no stated mechanism for delivering an own-session baseline, so §15's done-when ("the thirteen ids pass alone") is unreachable as written.
findings.text: §15's two exemptions leave two of the thirteen ids red: `tests/test_follower_survives_a_config_change.py::test_a_follower_defers_one_tick_and_keeps_delivering_across_a_config_error` and `tests/test_follower_survives_a_host_change.py::test_an_arm_with_no_checkpoint_replays_no_transitions_and_no_peer_rows` each fail because the pane withholds the run's own baseline row (kind `(None, "working")`) — measured here: `RowPolicy(own_session="s-mine").feed({...from_state: None, to_state: "working", session: "s-mine"})` returns `[]` — while exemption A requires kind `("starting"|"dispatched","working")` and exemption B is keyed on the session being *observed*, so neither reaches an own-session baseline; the plan's own "The own session's other rows stay as they are" then leaves it withheld. The plan also mis-describes these tests as feeding rows "each with a session and a from_state", but their failing row is a baseline with `from_state = None`.

findings.reason: a node reading the closing sentence literally would not deliver an observed session's no-`from_state` row, which the earlier sentence and exemption B's stated scope require, so the instruction must be reworded to name the start exemption as the one not widened on `from_state`.
